display.title: Episode 226: The Whispering Droplets, Rabbi Akiva's Story (Before Lag BaOmer)
display.summary_short: A week before Lag BaOmer: Hillel teaches the whole Torah on one foot, a Beis Yaakov class says the Shema, and Akiva learns from dripping water that it is never too late to learn Torah.
display.summary_long: Broadcast one week before Lag BaOmer, the yahrzeit of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and the day the plague among Rabbi Akiva's students ended. Uncle Yossi teaches that we must honor and respect one another. 'Love your fellow as yourself' is one of the Twelve Pesukim every Tzivos Hashem soldier says, and Rabbi Akiva called it a great rule of the Torah. He tells how Shammai sent away a man who asked to learn the whole Torah on one foot, while patient Hillel answered that loving your fellow is the whole Torah and the rest is its explanation. Unity through Torah is what Moshiach is waiting for. A second-grade class from a Brooklyn girls' school says the Shema, followed by a sponsor message. The story, 'Never Too Late', tells how Rachel begged her husband Akiva, already forty, to learn Torah. Unsure, he sat by a river and saw soft drops of water that had worn a hole in a hard rock, and understood that Torah could enter his heart too. He became the great Rabbi Akiva and gave Rachel the credit. The show ends with the first winners of the Sefer Torah drawing contest.
display.lesson: It is never too late to start learning Torah; little by little it softens even the hardest heart. Love every Jew, because that is the whole Torah.
